lessons.title: Two switch states, one inductor
lessons.physicalIntuition: The switch pair chooses the inductor's left-end voltage. The inductor current then rises or falls according to the voltage difference between switch node and output while the capacitor absorbs the mismatch with load current.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: For ideal positive-current CCM, high-side on gives vL = Vin - Vo and diL/dt = (Vin-Vo)/L; low-side on gives vL = -Vo and diL/dt = -Vo/L. Integrating over a period yields volt-second balance and Vo = D Vin under ideal assumptions.
lessons.modelingConsequence: A buck-phase block must compute vL from the actual switch state and output, not from a precomputed ripple formula. Current polarity and node-voltage sign must be testable.
assumptions: periodic steady state for conversion ratio
lessons.interaction: Current-path puzzle: high-side and low-side states
lessons.transferQuestion: At Vin = 10 V and Vo = 4 V, which slope has larger magnitude and why must their time-weighted areas still cancel?

lessons.title: Dead time, body diodes, and reverse current
lessons.physicalIntuition: Turning both gates off does not stop inductor current. Positive current commutates into the low-side body diode; negative current can commutate into the high-side body diode. An asynchronous diode blocks the reverse-current state, while a forced synchronous switch can permit it.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: During dead time use vL = vsw,clamp - Vo, with vsw,clamp selected by current sign and diode drop. The diode's unilateral constraint creates a zero-current interval in DCM; synchronous bidirectional conduction removes that constraint unless control emulates the diode.
lessons.modelingConsequence: Dead time needs a third switching state and sign-aware clamp. A model that always applies -Vo/L during dead time has the wrong negative-current path. Diode emulation needs a zero-current decision with delay/hysteresis assumptions.
assumptions: switch capacitance and reverse recovery excluded unless enabled
lessons.interaction: Current-path puzzle: dead time, asynchronous, reverse-current, and diode-emulation cases
lessons.transferQuestion: Which body diode conducts if iL is negative when both MOSFET gates turn off?

lessons.title: Charge balance and the input/output capacitors
lessons.physicalIntuition: The output capacitor is a local current reservoir: it charges when inductor current exceeds load and discharges when it is smaller. The input capacitor supplies the pulsed high-side current locally.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Write iC,out = iL - iload and integrate over a period to obtain zero net charge in steady state. The source/high-side current is a gated version of inductor current, so input-capacitor RMS is not equal to output ripple current.
lessons.modelingConsequence: Integrate the capacitor state from current mismatch; do not impose output ripple. Export capacitor current and source current as first-class signals for balance and RMS checks.
assumptions: periodic steady state for charge balance
lessons.interaction: Predict capacitor-current sign before revealing synchronized plots
lessons.transferQuestion: Immediately after a positive load step, before iL changes, what is the sign and magnitude change of capacitor current?
